chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Aqraʿ, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'God did not burden the servants beyond what they can bear.' He mentioned the obligatory duties and said: 'He only obligated them to fast for one month of the year, while they are capable of more than that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the rationale behind the obligation of fasting for only one month in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *lā yukallifu nafsahillā illā wus'ahā* by contrasting the general capacity of humans with specific divine legislation. He highlights that while fasting for longer than one month is physically possible, God prescribed only Ramadan to ensure the obligation remains a manageable burden (*yusr*) rather than an excessive strain, reinforcing the Shia understanding of divine mercy in legal rulings.
